$comment: u0 — FROZEN CONTRACT for plan 136 typing-grace-gate. PM-authored (pij-fellow-whale, 2026-09-05) before fan-out. Field spellings derived from crates/core/src/model.rs (Event, Envelope, SeatDescriptor, DeliveryOutcome, DeliveryOrigin), crates/core/src/wire.rs (EVENT_VERSION, KNOWN_EVENT_KINDS) and crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs (delivery.inbox-ack emission) — none invented. u1/u2/u3 fill this contract; widening it is a stop-and-ask to the PM. Rust structs serialize snake_case (no rename_all on SeatDescriptor); spine events are {v, at, kind, seat, payload} with `seq` skipped on the wire (model.rs Event).

grace.$comment: Seam (a): ONE definition. `pub const DEFAULT_TYPING_GRACE_MS: u64 = 60_000;` in crates/core/src/delivery.rs, overridable by env PIJ_TYPING_GRACE_MS at the daemon only. The extension NEVER restates 60000 except as the `??` fallback used solely when the daemon omits the field (AC7).

event_kinds.$comment: Both kinds MUST be added to KNOWN_EVENT_KINDS in crates/core/src/wire.rs (u2), otherwise a reader decodes them as WireEvent::Unknown. Existing sibling kinds for style: delivery.outcome, delivery.inbox-ack, delivery.pointer-parked.

held.$comment: Spine event appended when the extension declines to inject a claimed row because the human typed inside the grace. `since_ms` is the Unix-ms timestamp of the LAST observed keystroke, not the hold's start.

released.$comment: Appended when the grace elapsed and the extension injected + acked the row. `at_ms` is when the release decision was taken; the delivery.inbox-ack that follows is the delivered receipt (origin reader-read).

hold_request.$comment: Seam (b): POST /v1/hold, bearer-authed exactly like /v1/register. Additive route. u1 calls it, u2 serves it. AMENDED TWICE on 2026-09-05. (i) prime ruling (assets/inputs/ruling-hold-inversion-2026-09-05.md): serving it appends the `held` event AND RETURNS THE JOB TO PENDING with not_before = now + typing_grace_ms, so held means PENDING-AND-UNCLAIMED — nothing stays running to block a bypass claim (queue.rs:258), the 300 s claim lease is irrelevant, and re-offers are bounded and observable. (ii) PM ruling on u2's evidence: the row is carried by JOB_ID, not by a daemon-side (seat,msg_id) map. The extension already holds job_id from its InboxClaim, so passing it makes the daemon stateless here and removes a map whose failure mode was silent divergence across restarts. Idempotent per job_id: a repeat is 200 and appends nothing.

release_request.$comment: Seam (b): POST /v1/release. Appends the `released` event AND CLEARS THE DEFERRAL (not_before = now) so the extension's next ordinary claim gets the row immediately. AMENDED 2026-09-05 on u1's evidence: without un-deferral the row stays parked at hold_time + grace — about last_key + two graces — and AC1's 'injected at t0+60 s +/- 3 s' is unreachable. Carries job_id for the same reason hold does. Releasing a job that is not deferred is 200 with `released: false` — the extension must be free to release optimistically after a restart without a 4xx. AMENDED AGAIN 2026-09-05 (PM ruling on u2's stale-held finding): THE EVENT AND THE MUTATION ARE SEPARATE FACTS AND ARE REPORTED SEPARATELY. delivery.released is appended WHENEVER the extension declares a release — it is a claim about the EXTENSION's state ('I am no longer holding this'), which is what the readback projects — while the queue un-deferral is attempted independently and its outcome is reported in the body (released|not-deferred|absent|terminal). Without that split, the restart path leaves the sender staring at a stale hold forever: after a restart the extension has lost its in-memory note, claims and acks the row through the ordinary path, delivery succeeds, and nothing ever clears the held evidence. So the extension MUST call /v1/release before acking any row it may have held (unconditionally is fine and cheapest — the call is idempotent and every no-op is typed), and the daemon MUST append the event even when the row is running or already terminal.

register_response_with_grace.$comment: Seam (a) on the wire. The register route answers Envelope::ok("pij register", descriptor) (crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:399). `typing_grace_ms` is an ADDITIVE field on the response DATA object, flattened alongside the descriptor's snake_case fields — NOT a new field on SeatDescriptor (which would leak into seat.put rows and every registry projection). u2 defines the response wrapper in crates/core/src/wire.rs; u1 reads `accepted.typing_grace_ms`. Descriptor fields shown are the real ones from model.rs SeatDescriptor; absent Options are omitted by skip_serializing_if.

invariants.$comment: The properties every unit's tests must defend. These are the review priorities (impl-guide review.inputs).
invariants.held_is_unacked: A held row is PENDING-AND-UNCLAIMED and NEVER acked (amended 2026-09-05 by the hold inversion — it was 'CLAIMED but never acked' in the original draft; u3 caught the stale wording). Nothing may mark it delivered while held; killing the seat or the daemon must leave both rows in the store, pending, and re-register must redeliver them in id order (AC5).
invariants.order_preserved: Release drains in claim order — a message held at t0 is injected before one held at t0+1s.
invariants.bypass: Msg.command (compact|new|reload) and urgent payloads skip the hold entirely: inject + ack immediately, even with holds outstanding, and the held rows stay held (AC4).
invariants.one_grace: Exactly one numeric literal for the grace exists in Rust (DEFAULT_TYPING_GRACE_MS) and exactly one in TS (the `??` fallback). A test on each side asserts the observed value; a TS test asserts the wire value WINS over the fallback (AC7, risk r4).
invariants.no_false_typing: Programmatic edits (the extension's own inject/setEditorText) must not count as keystrokes — u1 ignores editor changes within 200 ms of its own write and tests it (risk r1).
invariants.no_double_delivery: A held row must not be re-delivered by the daemon's retry scheduler while held (risk r2).

receipt_note.$comment: PM finding 2026-09-05, evidence for the plan-vs-reality ruling: crates/daemon/src/delivery/mod.rs:249-251 routes Omp|Pi to DeliveryRung::Observe and :397-398 already emits Queued{reason:"extension-stream"} — the extension-stream push receipt is ALREADY queued-not-delivered on main, and flips to delivered only on delivery.inbox-ack (plan-134-live-proof.md spine rows seq 7-8, outcome reader-read). A repo-wide grep for `extension-stream` returns two hits, both inside delivery/mod.rs (:398 the producer, :1132 its own test) — risk r3's 'consumers that expected delivered' set is EMPTY. u2's receipt work is therefore a REGRESSION GUARD (a test pinning queued-before-ack / delivered-after-ack), not a behaviour change.

claim_note.$comment: RETRACTS the peek_request block of commit b7fe533a — my premise there was wrong and u2 disproved it from the source. Queue::peek (crates/store/src/queue.rs:315-319) selects the oldest row in state IN ('pending','running') with NO not_before condition, and its port doc promises exactly that (oldest LIVE, including claimed), so a deferred hold stays at the head of every peek and hides the bypass behind it. THE ORDINARY CLAIM PATH IS ALREADY CORRECT and needs nothing new: Queue::claim (queue.rs:253-259) filters `state = 'pending' AND not_before <= unixepoch()`, so a held row deferred to now + grace is SKIPPED and a newly-arrived command is returned instead. The extension therefore keeps claiming as it does today; no peek call, no new route.
claim_note.bypass_mechanism: queue.rs:253-259 — deferred rows are not claimable; the next eligible row is.

queue_seam.$comment: ADDED 2026-09-05 (PM ruling on u2's evidence, notified to prime). Queue::retry (queue.rs:345-374) updates only `WHERE id = ?1 AND state = 'running'` and deliberately ERRORS on a row nobody claimed, so it can serve /v1/hold (the row is running: the extension claimed it moments earlier) but CANNOT serve /v1/release, whose row is pending-and-deferred. That is a genuine API gap, not a held-state request. ONE additive port method closes it, with NO new stored state and NO schema change — which keeps prime's 'do not teach the store a held state' intact.
queue_seam.method: Queue::defer(job: JobId, delay: Duration) -> DeferOutcome  ·  Queue::release_deferred(job: JobId) -> ReleaseOutcome
queue_seam.semantics: Set a LIVE delivery row (pending OR running) to state='pending', worker/claimed_at cleared, not_before = now + delay. ATTEMPT IS NOT INCREMENTED: a hold is not a failed attempt, and inflating attempt would corrupt the backoff and budget logic that reads it. Absent or terminal job -> DeferOutcome::NotLive. AMENDED 2026-09-05 (prime): the routes still answer 200, but the BODY MUST NAME THE NO-OP AND ITS REASON — {held|released: false, noop: true, reason: "absent" | "terminal"} — because those two states have different meanings for the caller (an absent job on release is a CALLER BUG; a terminal one is benign) and collapsing them into one silent 200 leaves the instrument unable to separate them. Test BOTH branches.
queue_seam.used_by: /v1/hold calls defer(job, typing_grace_ms). /v1/release calls release_deferred(job) — NOT defer(job, 0). AMENDED 2026-09-05 on u2's race analysis: an unconditional defer(job, ZERO) on a DUPLICATE release revokes a claim the extension is currently executing, so its ack then fails and the body can be injected a second time — the exact double delivery this plan exists to prevent, shipped inside the fix. release_deferred is therefore PENDING-ONLY and atomic: it clears not_before on a pending delivery row, leaves a RUNNING row untouched and says so, and never becomes a check-then-mutate (a route that is correct only when nothing else is happening is not correct).
queue_seam.fence: u2 += crates/core/src/ports.rs, crates/store/src/queue.rs, the testkit queue fake, and those crates' own tests.

outcomes.defer: Deferred | NotLive{reason: absent|terminal} — 200 with {held:false, noop:true, reason} on NotLive.
outcomes.release_deferred: Released{recipient,msg_id} | NotDeferred (the row is RUNNING — a live reader owns it; 200 with {released:false, noop:true, reason:'not-deferred'}) | NotLive{reason: absent|terminal} (200 with {released:false, noop:true, reason}). Three distinguishable states, because an absent job is a caller bug, a terminal one is benign, and a running one means the reader already has it — collapsing any of them loses the fact the operator needs.

recovery_peek.$comment: ADDED 2026-09-05 (PM ruling on u2's ordering counterexample). AC5 promises held rows come back IN ORDER after a restart, and that does NOT fall out of the queue by itself: Queue::claim orders only ELIGIBLE rows, so an older row re-held to a later deadline loses its place to a newer row whose deferral has already elapsed (u2's counterexample: job1 deferred to 120 s, job2 due at 61 s, restart at 61 s -> claim returns job2 first). The extension has lost its in-memory notes, so it cannot release job1 by id. Queue::peek is the ONE call that can see it: it returns the oldest LIVE row regardless of not_before (queue.rs:315-319) — the very property that made it wrong for typing-path polling makes it exactly right for recovery.
recovery_peek.when: session_start ONLY, after re-register, before ordinary claiming resumes. NEVER on the typing/bypass path — that remains the ordinary claim, which filters not_before.
recovery_peek.loop: peek -> if it returns a row, POST /v1/release for that job_id (clearing its deferral and its held evidence) -> claim -> inject+ack -> repeat until peek returns nothing deferred. Each pass takes the oldest live row, so FIFO is restored by construction rather than assumed.
recovery_peek.fence: u1 re-adds peekInbox to adapters/daemon-http.ts for this purpose only; u2 adds nothing — /v1/inbox?peek=true already exists.
recovery_peek.witness: Restart with two held rows whose deferrals differ (the older deferred LATER) must deliver them oldest-first. Assert the order, not merely that both arrived.
